title: Review the pattern, not just the score
summary: When a session goes badly, improvement usually comes from identifying one repeatable execution pattern to test next session instead of reacting only to the score outcome.
why: Outcome-only review turns bad sessions into emotion without producing a useful testable change.
Process review converts frustration into one concrete adjustment the player can try immediately.
actions: After the block, write one sentence for why the misses happened, one sentence for the repeated pattern, and one sentence for what you will test next session.
Pick one process goal for the next session instead of trying to fix every flaw at once.
Judge progress by whether the repeated execution error appears less often, not only by whether the PB moved.
avoid: Do not treat one bad benchmark day as proof that all progress disappeared.

drills.reason: A simple review loop keeps the next session actionable instead of emotional.

evidence.claim: Improvement comes from process-based reflection and appropriately difficult practice, not only from staring at the outcome.
evidence.excerpt: The Voltaic mentality article emphasizes review through controllable process changes.
